name: Tabwise
author: tinotines

sections.description:
Tabwise organizes your WordPress Pages and Posts into tabs.

Once a site grows past a few dozen pages or posts, the admin list turns into one long scroll. Finding the right page means searching, paging and squinting at titles. Tabwise adds a row of color-coded tabs above your Pages and Posts lists. Group your content into tabs like “Services,” “Locations,” “Legal” or “Tutorials,” click a tab, and the list shows only what’s in it.

Tabwise only sorts. It never creates, edits, publishes or deletes your pages or posts.

Free and open source, forever. Every feature is included. There’s no pro version, no locked features, no upsells, no ads, no tracking and no branding added to your dashboard.

If Tabwise saves you time and you’d like to say thanks, you can buy me a coffee. It’s never expected.

Pages features

  • Tabs above the Pages list. Click a tab to see only its pages. Switching tabs is instant, with no page reload, and the list keeps its full width.
  • All and Unassigned. “All” shows every page, and “Unassigned” shows the pages you haven’t filed yet.
  • Default tab. Pin any tab and it opens first whenever you visit Pages.
  • Lock tabs. Lock a tab from its ⋯ menu so it can’t be moved or deleted by accident. A small lock icon shows on locked tabs.
  • Colors. A full color picker with hue, opacity, Hex, RGB and HSL, preset colors and your own saved colors.
  • Icons. Over 100 built-in icons with search (try “phone”, “legal” or “shop”), plus optional custom icons by upload or link, including Google Fonts icons.
  • Always readable. Tab labels get strong contrast automatically, whatever color you pick, in light and dark admin themes.
  • Drag and drop. Reorder tabs by dragging them, including into and out of the “more tabs” list. A blue marker shows exactly where the tab will land.
  • Move pages your way. Use Bulk actions, the Tab field in Quick Edit, or drag a page onto a tab.
  • More tabs. Extra tabs sit behind a “more tabs” button. Each one keeps its color and its own ⋯ menu.
  • Manage Tabs (Pages → Manage Tabs). Every page tab in one table: rename, recolor, change icons, reorder, set the default, filter, sort A–Z, or select several and change, merge or delete them at once.
  • Tab layouts for pages. Start in one click with 8 ready-made sets: Business & Services, Local Contractor, Online Store, Blog or Magazine, Agency or Portfolio, Restaurant & Hospitality, Software & SaaS, and Nonprofit & Community.
  • Your own layouts. Save your current page tabs as a layout or build one from scratch, then edit, apply or delete it any time.
  • Import and export. Save your page tabs and layouts to a file and load them on another site, including which pages go in each tab (matched by page address).

Posts features

Turn on Posts in Tabwise Settings and the Posts screen gets every feature above, with its own separate set of tabs. Post tabs never mix with page tabs.

  • Tabs above the Posts list, with All, Unassigned, a default tab, locked tabs and the “more tabs” list.
  • The same colors, icons, drag and drop, Quick Edit field and Bulk actions as Pages.
  • Manage Tabs (Posts → Manage Tabs). The full table, bulk actions, filtering and sorting, just for post tabs.
  • Tab layouts for posts. 8 ready-made sets made for posts: General Blog, Company Blog, Local Business Blog, Tech & Tutorials, Food & Recipes, Travel, Lifestyle & Personal, and Podcast & Video.
  • Your own post layouts, plus import and export, kept separate from your page layouts.
  • Zero cost when off. If Posts is turned off, Tabwise loads nothing at all on the Posts screen.

Admin settings

One settings page covers both Pages and Posts: Pages → Tabwise Settings, also linked from the Posts menu.

  • Screens. Pages are always on. Turn Posts on or off.
  • Visible tabs. Choose how many tabs show in the bar, from 3 to 10. The rest go under “more tabs.”
  • Custom icons. Off by default. Turn it on to upload your own icons or import them from a link.
  • Who can use tabs. Administrators always have access. Choose which other roles can use and manage tabs. People can only move content they’re already allowed to edit.
  • Uninstall. Choose whether deleting the plugin also removes your tabs and settings. Your pages and posts are never touched either way.

Safe by design

Tabwise only sorts. It never creates, edits, publishes, trashes or deletes your pages or posts. Deleting a tab simply moves its content to Unassigned.

Lightweight

  • Loads only on the Pages and Posts list screens and the Manage Tabs pages, and never on the front end of your site.
  • One small script and one small stylesheet, with no jQuery, frameworks, icon fonts or external requests.
  • Uses WordPress’s own taxonomy system, with no custom database tables.
  • Built-in icons use WordPress’s own icon set, which is already loaded in your dashboard. Custom icons are resized in your browser and saved with the tab, so nothing is added to your Media Library.

Made for the open source community

Tabwise was made with love for the WordPress and open source community by tinocast. It was vibe coded (built with the help of AI) and is actively maintained with long-term support (LTS). Bug reports and ideas are always welcome in the support forum.

External services

Tabwise makes no outside requests on its own. Only if you turn on custom icons and choose “Import from URL”, your browser downloads the icon from the link you paste, once, at that moment:

  • For Google Fonts icon links, the icon file is downloaded from Google Fonts (fonts.gstatic.com). No personal data is sent. See Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
  • For any other link, the image is downloaded from the site you pasted.

The icon is then saved inside your site. If a site doesn’t allow its image to be copied, Tabwise uses the link itself, and that image loads from that site when your tabs are shown.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for “Tabwise”, or upload the plugin zip.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Go to Pages and click “+ New tab” to create your first tab, or open Pages → Manage Tabs → Tab layouts to start from a ready-made set.
  4. Optional: visit Pages → Tabwise Settings to turn on Posts, choose how many tabs show, turn on custom icons or choose which user roles can use tabs.
sections.faq:
Is it really free?

Yes. Every feature is free and will stay free. There is no pro version.

Does it work for Posts too?

Yes. Turn on Posts in Pages → Tabwise Settings. Posts get every feature Pages have, with their own separate tabs, layouts and Manage Tabs page.

Can deleting a tab delete my pages or posts?

No. Tabwise never deletes, trashes or edits your content. When you delete a tab, its content becomes Unassigned.

Can a page be in more than one tab?

No. Each page or post lives in exactly one tab, or in Unassigned. That keeps counts accurate and moving content simple.

Does it slow down my site?

No. Nothing loads on the front end. In the admin it only loads on the Pages and Posts lists and the Manage Tabs pages.

Who can see and manage tabs?

Administrators, plus any roles you allow under Pages → Tabwise Settings. People can only move content they’re already allowed to edit.

What happens to my data if I uninstall?

By default your tabs are kept in case you reinstall. To remove everything, check “Remove all tabs and settings when the plugin is deleted” in Pages → Tabwise Settings before deleting the plugin. Your pages and posts are never touched either way.

What happens to images I upload as icons?

They never reach your server. Your browser shrinks the image to a small 64×64 icon and only that tiny icon (usually a few kilobytes) is saved with your tabs. Nothing is added to your Media Library or uploads folder, and the original file stays on your computer.

Can I use Google’s Material icons?

Yes. Turn on custom icons in Pages → Tabwise Settings, open a tab’s icon picker, choose “Import from URL” and paste the link from the Google Fonts icons page (select an icon first so the link includes it). The icon takes your tab’s color.

Can I move my tabs to another site?

Yes. In Manage Tabs, click Export to download your tabs and saved layouts, then Import the file on the other site. Pages and posts are put back in their tabs when their addresses match.

Does it work with Elementor and other page builders?

Yes. Tabwise works on the standard WordPress Pages and Posts lists, so it works no matter how your content is built.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • New: Lock a tab from its ⋯ menu (or in Manage Tabs). Locked tabs show a small lock icon and can’t be dragged or deleted until you unlock them.
  • Improved: Switching tabs is now instant. Tabs are loaded ahead of time, so the list appears right away.
  • Fixed: Duplicating or trashing a page or post (including with other plugins like Duplicate Page) no longer sends you back to a different tab. You stay in the tab you were in, and the copy shows up there.

1.0.1

  • New: Pages → Manage Tabs and Posts → Manage Tabs pages for viewing and editing all tabs at once, including bulk color, icon, merge and delete.
  • New: Choose how many tabs show in the bar (3 to 10) in Pages → Tabwise Settings.
  • New: Drag tabs into and out of the “more tabs” list.
  • New: Over 100 built-in icons with search, plus optional custom icons by upload or link.
  • New: Tab layouts library with 8 page layouts and 8 post layouts.
  • New: Create your own tab layouts (blank or from your current tabs) and edit, apply or delete them.
  • New: Import and export tabs and your saved layouts, including which pages belong to each tab.
  • New: Tabs in the “more tabs” list have their own ⋯ menu and keep their colors.
  • New: Saved custom icons you can reuse, with an option to remove them.
  • New: Import icons from Google Fonts icon page links.
  • New: RGB and HSL color modes now have a slider and a full-size input for each value.
  • Improved: Tab labels now always have strong contrast, in light and dark admin themes and with any tab color.
  • Improved: The color picker always opens in Hex.
  • Fixed: New tabs are now added left to right in the order you create them.
  • Fixed: Moving pages no longer jumps you back to page 1 of the list, which made rows look like they disappeared.
  • Fixed: Bulk actions and filters could go missing after switching from an empty tab.
  • Settings moved from Settings → Tabwise to Pages → Tabwise Settings (also linked from the Posts menu when Posts is enabled).

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
